content.title: About
content.content: Cucumber is an annual herbaceous plant of the gourd family cultivated for its edible fruit. The fruits have a crisp, juicy flesh, a mildly sweet flavor and a refreshing aroma. Cucumbers are commonly used fresh in salads, sandwiches, snacks and drinks.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cucumbers are about 95 % water, making them an excellent way to stay hydrated.
There are over 100 varieties of cucumber, including long, short, sweet and pickling types.
Cucumbers were cultivated in ancient Egypt more than 4,000 years ago.
Cucumbers contain compounds such as cucurbitacin that may have anti‑inflammatory effects.
The edible seeds are a source of beneficial fatty acids.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: The high water content helps maintain the body’s fluid balance, especially in hot weather.

items.title: Low Calorie
items.content: Cucumbers are low in calories, making them a suitable food for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Vitamins and Minerals
items.content: Cucumbers provide vitamins K, C and B‑complex, as well as potassium, magnesium and silica, which support skin and bone health.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Flavonoids and carotenoids in cucumbers help combat free radicals and reduce oxidative stress.

items.title: Digestive Support
items.content: Fiber, especially in the skin, promotes regular bowel movements and helps prevent constipation.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to cucumbers, manifested as itching, swelling or hives.

items.title: Pesticide Residues
items.content: Unwashed cucumbers can carry pesticide residues; it is advisable to rinse thoroughly or choose organic varieties.

items.title: Stomach Sensitivity
items.content: People with a sensitive stomach may experience gas or discomfort when consuming large amounts of cucumber.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cucumbers are typically eaten raw—sliced into salads, sandwiches, wraps, or as a snack with dip. They can be pickled, used in cold soups such as gazpacho, or blended into smoothies for a refreshing taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cucumbers in the refrigerator’s vegetable drawer, wrapped in a paper towel or a perforated bag. When stored properly they stay fresh for 5‑7 days. Keep them away from ethylene‑producing fruits, as this accelerates spoilage.
